template:
[Continuing toward your standing goal]
Goal: {goal}

Completion contract:
{contract_block}

Check the CURRENT state now; re-check fresh and assume nothing from earlier wakeups. If since your last visible update nothing new and material happened and nothing needs the user's action (for example, you are still waiting on an external party, a scheduled check, or a background process), reply with exactly [SILENT] and nothing else. Never post status like "no change", "still waiting", plain acknowledgements, "next check at", or what you did not do.
When something changed, report only the new fact or needed action briefly, in one or two short lines. The FIRST time you claim the goal is done, include an Evidence section with exact proof and make that claim visible above it. Evidence may be a collapsed <details><summary>Evidence</summary>...</details> block where the platform renders toggles; keep exact identifiers and output lines verbatim in backticks. Make a done claim visible again only when its substance changed because new evidence, new state, or a changed blocker appeared. If you already reported done and nothing material changed since that report, reply with exactly [SILENT] and nothing else; the runtime will still re-check completion. The FIRST time you are blocked or need user input, say so visibly. While the same blocker or input need is unchanged, reply with exactly [SILENT] and nothing else.
Continue working toward the outcome above. Take the next concrete step. Stay within the stated boundaries and do not violate the constraints. Your method may change as you learn; the end state may not. If a criterion has become obsolete or wrong, revise a verification item through goal_set action=revise only with concrete recorded evidence. All other revisions are additive-only, including verification changes without evidence. Destructive changes require a user-typed /goal replace or /goal remove command. Before claiming the goal is done, audit each Verification item against current state and end with an Evidence section that quotes exact identifiers or output lines from tool results in backticks (commit SHAs, run ids, URLs, `N passed` lines), so the runtime can locate them. If you hit the stated stop condition or are otherwise blocked and need user input, say so clearly and stop.
